definition: CausalCriterionConcrete hasCausalPower x := ∃ w, hasCausalPower w x: concrete iff it has causal power at some world. This is the causal-inefficacy criterion of the Way of Negation read from the concrete side. It is a sibling sense, NOT the definition of concreteness used by the owner's principle.
note: SEP 'Abstract Objects' (SEP-ABSTRACT-OBJECTS-2020-CRITERIA) §3.2 calls this the most widely accepted version of the Way of Negation and records objections: epiphenomenal qualia, abstract artifacts as effects, Lewis's events as sets, and the unsolved participation problem. If adopted as the definition, the owner's principle STMT-CAUSAL-POWER-AND-ACTIVITY-REQUIRE-CONCRETENESS would hold by definition (premise smuggling, invariant 9). Navigation citation, no claim.
